observed_local_evidence.failure_phase: First compiled transport execution, at block_until_ready, inside host callback implementation
observed_local_evidence.exception: jax.debug.callback failed to find a local CPU device to place the inputs on. Make sure cpu is listed in JAX_PLATFORMS.

verdict.source_support: Explicitly initialize both backends; require both initialization successes; first-listed TPU wins default priority; callback can explicitly select local CPU without adding CPU to default TPU device enumeration.

source_references.finding: Callback implementation explicitly selects local CPU device, places callback arguments there, and uses temporary CPU/empty-mesh context.
TPU host callback closure invokes debug_callback implementation.
Explicit backend list controls initialization, descending priority, and fail-loud behavior for every listed backend.
Documented explicit-list semantics: first platform default, all listed initialization required.
Backend lookup uses explicit or deprecated override platform; missing CPU in initialized map raises; absent override selects default backend.
Default device enumeration and counts delegate to a single selected backend, not a union.
Local devices and process count use the requested/default backend.
Default-device context uses thread-local state and restores previous state on exit.
Default-device configuration independently affects ordinary JAX placement.
Ordinary default device may be overridden independently of selected default backend.
Environment used to initialize configuration state.
Initialized backend state is reused; editing environment later is not a valid backend recovery.
True multi-platform lowering is separate and unsupported; partitioned transport remains unsupported on TPU.
Compiled TPU platform uses ordinary TPU send/receive transport independently of host CPU backend availability.
